assistant_rules.note: Suggest whatever helps, wording or ideas, as suggestions I can accept or reject. Never change my draft directly. You can submit when I say a draft is final.

assignments.title: Short paper 1: Is lying ever permitted?
assignments.prompt: Defend an answer to the question, using one example and answering one objection. About 800 words.

assignments.title: Field report 1: Leaf litter in the campus woods
assignments.prompt: Report your group's leaf-litter transect: question, method, results and what they suggest. About 500 words.

assignments.title: Short paper 2: Do we owe anything to future generations?
assignments.prompt: Defend a position on whether we have duties to people who do not exist yet, and answer the strongest objection. About 1,000 words in the final paper; bring a 400-word draft to peer review.

sentences.text: Lying is permitted when telling the truth would cause serious harm to an innocent person.
sentences.author: student

sentences.text: Kant famously disagreed, but most people's intuitions are on my side.
sentences.author: student

sentences.text: Imagine a friend hiding in your house from someone who wants to hurt them.
sentences.author: student

sentences.text: If the attacker asks where your friend is, lying is obviously right.
sentences.author: student

sentences.text: Honesty matters because people need to trust each other, but trust is not more important than a life.
sentences.author: student

sentences.text: Some will say that allowing one lie makes every lie easier.
sentences.author: student

sentences.text: That is a slippery slope, and it does not follow.
sentences.author: student

sentences.text: We measured the depth of leaf litter at ten points along a transect from the main path into the woods.
sentences.author: student

sentences.text: Litter was deeper farther from the path, which shows that foot traffic breaks it down.
sentences.author: student

sentences.text: Depth ranged from 1.5 cm near the path to 6 cm at the far end.
sentences.author: student

sentences.text: We did not measure soil moisture or count the trees near each point.
sentences.author: student

sentences.text: We owe future generations at least a world that is no worse than the one we were given.
sentences.author: student

sentences.text: People who are not born yet cannot vote or complain, but that does not make their interests count for less.
sentences.author: student

sentences.text: If anything, they are more vulnerable, because they depend entirely on choices made before they arrive.
sentences.author: student

sentences.text: Their claim on us is like the claim of a stranger in another country: real, even if we never meet them.
sentences.author: student

sentences.text: Most philosophers now accept some version of this view.
sentences.author: student

sentences.text: Think about a city that builds a dam it knows will fail in eighty years.
sentences.author: student

sentences.text: Nobody alive today will be hurt when it fails, but we would still say the builders did something wrong.
sentences.author: student

sentences.text: Engineers who cut corners on purpose would not be excused because their victims were born later, and we would blame them even more if they had simply saved money.
sentences.author: student

sentences.text: The harm is real even though the people harmed do not exist yet, this shows that time alone does not cancel a duty.
sentences.author: student

sentences.text: Parfit's non-identity problem is the strongest objection.
sentences.author: student

sentences.text: Our choices change which people are born, so the people of the future cannot complain that we made them worse off, without our choices they would not exist at all.
sentences.author: student

sentences.text: Parfit himself thought the problem was real and spent years looking for a principle that avoids it.
sentences.author: student

sentences.text: If no particular person is made worse off, it can seem that no one is wronged.
sentences.author: student

sentences.text: I think this objection is clever but it does not change what we should do.
sentences.author: student

sentences.text: Climate policy is the clearest case.
sentences.author: student

sentences.text: Every ton of carbon we burn now makes storms and droughts worse for people a century from now.
sentences.author: student

sentences.text: Sea walls, crop failures and heat waves will fall hardest on people who had no say in our choices.
sentences.author: student

sentences.text: Cutting emissions costs us something today, but the cost to them is much larger.
sentences.author: student

sentences.text: Even a small chance of these harms should count, because so many people will live through them.
sentences.author: student

sentences.text: So we do owe something to future generations.
sentences.author: student

sentences.text: What we owe is not everything we have, but at least a world no worse than ours (Parfit 1984).
sentences.author: student

sentences.text: That is a modest duty, and it is one we are failing.
sentences.author: student

sentences.text: Recycling and voting are not enough; the duty asks for real limits on what we take.
sentences.author: student

comments.quote: most people's intuitions are on my side
comments.text: How do you know? Give an example or a source, or argue for the claim instead.

comments.quote: That is a slippery slope, and it does not follow.
comments.text: Naming a fallacy is not a reply. Explain why one lie need not lead to more.

comments.quote: which shows that foot traffic breaks it down
comments.text: Your data show a pattern, not its cause. What else could explain it?

comments.quote: Depth ranged from 1.5 cm near the path to 6 cm at the far end.
comments.text: Report every point in a table, not just the range.

comments.quote: Think about a city that builds a dam
comments.text: Great example. Can you say why the builders knew it would fail?

comments.quote: What we owe is not everything we have
comments.text: This is clearer than your first sentence. Could your thesis say it this way?

comments.quote: Most philosophers now accept some version of this view.
comments.text: Who? Cite someone, or argue for the view instead of counting heads.

comments.quote: I think this objection is clever but it does not change what we should do.
comments.text: This is the heart of the paper. Why doesn't it change what we should do?

comments.quote: the cost to them is much larger
comments.text: Larger by what measure? Give one concrete comparison.

comments.quote: do not exist yet, this shows
comments.text: Comma splice: split this into two sentences.
Run-on sentence; a period after 'worse off' would help.
Add the page number, as the syllabus asks.
